Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

vellumwidget 0.15.0.9000

  • Constant-size marks are hit and ringed where they are drawn (VW-42). Under axis zoom, text and point glyphs keep their pixel size, but hover, click picking and the hover and selection rings of raster mode’s canvas tiers used their record boxes scaled by the zoom: at 4x a label answered the pointer far past its ink and its ring was four times too big. The hit test and the rings now use each mark’s box at its 1x size about its anchor (a label’s anchor from its run’s SVG, a glyph’s centre). The nearest-mark fallback in SVG mode uses the same boxes. Known limit: a glyph cut by a mask (clip_layer()) keeps its 1x cut in raster mode, where SVG mode moves the mask edge with the zoom; brushing and lasso still test the record boxes.

  • Two layers’ conditions on one selection keep apart (VP-72). A point layer and a text layer each colouring by condition(sel, ..., if_false) shared one condition tag, so a non-selected point took the text layer’s if_false (whichever condition came last), in SVG and raster mode. The runtime now styles a condition’s elements by the tag vellumplot sends ("<sel>:<aes>@<layer>" for such layers), and falls back to "<sel>:<aes>" for an older vellumplot.

  • Rotated text keeps its rotation under axis zoom (VW-41). In SVG mode, with axis zoom active (even at 1x), rotated mark_text(angle =) labels and rotated annotation text were drawn unrotated: the constant-size text code read only the matrix() of vellum’s matrix(...) rotate(...) transform. The whole transform list is now composed, so a label keeps its rotation and still holds its pixel size about its anchor. Rotated axis tick labels (theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle =))) are re-ticked rotated, with vellum’s anchoring, in SVG and raster mode alike, instead of flat and centred; exports follow. Raster mode’s text marks were already rotated (they are images).

  • Compact coordinates in raster mode (VR-18). With a vellum whose scene_display_list() takes precision, the display list’s coordinates ship quantised: each column (point centres and radii, rects, path vertices) as 16-bit integers within its range (24-bit for a column spanning more than 655 px), so no coordinate is off by more than 0.005 px, the precision of the SVG vellum writes for SVG mode and for raster mode’s axes. A 200k-point keyed scatter’s payload goes from 2.72 to 1.65 MB; decoding is no slower. The marks stay within half a pixel of their float positions up to 100x zoom, and drift as in SVG mode beyond. render_options(precision = "f32") keeps 32-bit floats, and the runtime reads float lists from an older vellum as before.

  • Smaller raster payloads for keys and numbered tooltips (VW-40). The element key column ships its integer differences as a bit-packed binary column (big jumps and restarts as exceptions) instead of a JSON array: a 200k keyed scatter’s keys go from 0.41 to 0.14 MB (1M: 2.0 to 0.7 MB). Tooltip templates now also take zero-padded and decimal numbers ("id 00042", "t = 0.05 s", "1.5e-07"): a digit run with leading zeros ships its width, so the text comes back byte for byte, and the number streams can ship as binary too. 200k tooltips sprintf("id %06d", id): 2.40 to 0.14 MB; "<b>g</b><br>x = 0.1234<br>y = -1.0567": 8.2 to 1.9 MB. Hover text is unchanged. Keys that are not mostly integers, or integers of more than 15 digits, ship as text as before.

  • With a vellum whose raster backend no longer isolates plain groups (VR-21), a blend-mode layer wrapped in a group without opacity, mask, blend or effect gets the mixed tier and composites with its mode, instead of falling back to the full mark PNG. vellumplot doesn’t emit such groups today; nothing changes in the runtime, which already composites any blend mode vellum reports.

  • State on one flagged mark leaves the rest of its run untouched (VW-37). When a condition, filter, dimming or legend hide/mute touched a mark drawn from a run image (VW-33), the browser re-rendered the whole run from its SVG, so the run’s other labels shifted slightly against vellum’s rendering. Now only the touched marks’ boxes (and those of marks overlapping them) are re-rendered and composited over the run’s PNG; every other mark keeps vellum’s pixels. A hidden mark with nothing else in its box is simply cleared, with no re-render. Also, constant-size marks under axis zoom (VW-35) take their slices from a full-size copy of the run PNG, so the first frame after a zoom is as sharp as later ones.

  • Flagged text and glyphs keep their size under axis zoom (VW-35). In raster mode, the marks drawn from a run image (keyed text, masked or patterned point glyphs; VW-30) used to grow with the zoom, while SVG mode keeps text and glyphs at their pixel size. In the mid and detail tiers and in exports, each such mark is now drawn at its anchor at constant size: from its slice of vellum’s run PNG, or, where marks overlap or a condition restyles one, from an atlas the browser rasterises once from the run’s SVG. The rest of a run (masked shapes, say) still scales with the zoom. render_options(zoom_marks = "scale") keeps the old behaviour.

  • Facets panned past their data stay empty in raster mode (VW-36). Panning isn’t clamped, so under axis zoom a facet or composition cell can be panned beyond its own data. In raster mode each panel drew the whole mark image (and any run of flagged marks spanning several panels) through its own transform, clipped only to its fixed rect on screen, so a neighbouring panel’s marks showed through. Each copy is now also clipped to the panel’s own area, in every tier (overview image, mid-tier canvas, detail tier) and in exports, as SVG mode always did.

vellumwidget 0.15.0

  • Requires vellum (>= 0.12.0).

  • Smaller tooltips in raster payloads (VW-38). Raster mode ships the element table’s string columns more compactly. Tooltips that follow a pattern around an integer (“pt 1”, “pt 2”, …, "<b>id 17</b><br>...") ship as a few templates plus their numbers, and the numbers not at all when they are the mark’s key. Repeated values (a dictionary) ship their codes bit-packed. Hover shows exactly the same tooltip text and HTML. For a 200,000-point scatter in raster mode: “pt N” tooltips 5.01 MB -> 2.72 MB (the tooltips themselves from 2.3 MB to under 1 kB), a repeated four-value tooltip 3.12 MB -> 2.82 MB, HTML tooltips 3.63 MB -> 3.17 MB.

  • Faster raster widget builds (VW-39). The legend membership (and the condition and filter tags) of a raster widget is built in its final, flat form instead of as one list entry per mark that was then flattened again. Building a 200,000-point scatter with a colour legend went from 1.12 s to 0.99 s, and 1,000,000 points from 4.7 s to 4.1 s. The payload is unchanged.

  • Smaller raster payloads: each key ships once (VR-22). With a vellum whose scene_display_list() takes keys = (feature-detected), the display list’s records point into the element table’s keys instead of carrying a second copy of every key. A 200,000-point keyed scatter in raster mode shrinks from 3.78 MB to 2.72 MB (6.07 MB to 5.01 MB with tooltips). Hover, selection, conditions, filters, the detail and mixed tiers and export work as before. With an older vellum the list keeps its own keys. Integer keys of 100,000 or more no longer keep a redundant bounding box in the payload.

  • Faster widget builds for big keyed plots (VR-19). as_widget() reads the element meta (tooltips, legend membership, conditions, interval values, …) as columns from vellum::scene_model(meta = "columns") instead of one record per element. Building a raster widget of a 200,000-point scatter with tooltips and a colour legend went from 1.5 s to 1.0 s, and 1,000,000 points from 8.4 s to 4.0 s (with vellumplot 0.17.0.9000, which writes the meta as columns). The payload is unchanged. Needs vellum 0.11.1.9000 or later.

vellumwidget 0.14.1

  • Raster mode: a blend mode no longer keeps the whole plot on the mark image (VW-32). One mark under a blend mode (a layer blend = "multiply", "screen", …) used to send every mark back to the PNG. The PNG also blended only against the other marks, not the panel beneath, so it didn’t match the static render. With a vellum that reports each run’s blend mode (run_blend, feature-detected), a blended run is drawn on a canvas layer of its own with that CSS mix-blend-mode, stacked between the marks before and after it. It blends with the furniture and marks beneath it, as SVG mode and scene_png() do, in every raster tier (the overview included, where the canvas now stands in for the PNG) and in PNG/SVG exports. In the detail tier the run’s <use> carries the blend mode. An older vellum, or a run vellum can’t composite, keeps the old behaviour.

  • Raster mode: conditions, filters, dimming and legend hide/mute reach the marks drawn from images (VW-33). Since 0.14.0, masked, patterned and similar marks and keyed text are drawn from one small PNG per run, with their look baked in. So a cross-filter could not hide a keyed label, and a condition() could not recolour or dim it, in the overview, mid and detail tiers or in exports. Each run now also ships as SVG. When some state touches a run’s marks, the widget applies it to that SVG, as SVG mode styles its nodes, and draws the result in place of the PNG; untouched runs keep their PNG. The re-rendered run is drawn by the browser, so its text can differ slightly from vellum’s. If the runs’ SVGs would exceed 4 MB, they are left out with a message, and those marks keep their own look.

  • Raster mode: a flagged run’s image is placed once per panel (VW-34). In the detail tier, a run of flagged marks (e.g. text labels) spanning a panel with a pan group and one without (a polar or coord_trans() panel in a composition) was drawn twice over the first panel, so its labels came out heavier. The root copy is now clipped to the marks it stands for. Under axis zoom, a run’s marks in a panel the zoom does not transform are drawn untransformed, like the exact marks there, instead of not at all. vellumplot does not produce that case today (raster axis zoom needs every mark panel to have a pan group), so this is a safeguard.

vellumwidget 0.14.0

  • Raster mode: one mark the display list can’t draw no longer keeps every mark on the PNG (VW-30). Masked marks (clip_to() / set_mask()), effects, hatches, patterns, repeating gradients, gradient strokes and keyed text used to keep the whole plot on the mark image: zoomed in, every mark stayed blurry and there was no detail tier. With a vellum that renders those marks as their own layer (scene_png(layer = "keyed_flagged"), feature-detected), the widget ships one small PNG per run of them in paint order and draws the rest exactly, compositing each run where it falls. So the other marks reach the crisp canvas and the SVG detail tier, and a label drawn after the points stays on top of them. The flagged marks themselves stay images: they are as sharp as the mark PNG and keep their own colours under condition() and dimming, though they still take the pointer and show a selection outline in the detail tier. Marks under a blend mode, more than 8 runs, or an older vellum: unchanged.

  • The navigator’s mini-map draws gridlines, ticks and reference lines visibly (VW-31). It squashes the whole plot into a short strip, and the strokes squashed with it, so horizontal gridlines and thin rules shrank to a fraction of a pixel and nearly disappeared. The mini-map’s strokes now keep their own width on screen (vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke), with a 1 px minimum.

  • SVG and PNG exports from SVG mode show condition dimming and selection outlines (VW-28). The widget styles these through CSS classes, and the page stylesheet does not travel with an exported SVG, so a condition() spotlight or a click selection exported undimmed and unoutlined. The export now writes those styles inline (dim opacity, selection stroke, legend mute, hidden filtered marks), resolved from the live theme, so the export matches the screen. Hover and keyboard focus stay out of the export.

  • Raster mode: a point or circle keeps its size when zooming crosses from the canvas tier to the SVG detail tier (VW-29). Without axis zoom (raw vellum scenes, polar and void panels), the whole scene zooms through its viewBox, and the detail tier’s nodes and the SVG mode grow with it. The mid tier’s canvas, however, drew point records and strokes at their unzoomed pixel size, so a large circle_grob() disc jumped in size between tiers. The canvas now follows the same rule: under viewBox zoom, glyphs and stroke widths scale with the view; under axis zoom they keep their pixel size, as before. Dense raw-scene scatters therefore show bigger dots at the mid zoom than they used to, matching the SVG mode.

  • Gradients, path clips and translucent groups no longer keep a raster plot out of the exact tiers (VW-23). With a vellum that has display list version 2 (scene_display_list(version = 2), feature-detected), gradient fills (linear_gradient() / radial_gradient(), pad extension), clips by a path and marks inside an opacity group are listed exactly. They are drawn on the zoomed canvas (a group as one layer at its opacity), take condition() / filter_by() styling (a condition colour replaces a gradient), become SVG nodes in the detail tier (<linearGradient> / <radialGradient>, chained <clipPath>s, <g opacity>) and export sharp. Older vellum: unchanged (those marks stay in the image). Masks (clip_to(), set_mask()), blend modes, effects, hatches and patterns still stay in the image.

  • Keyed marks that paint nothing (pick-only hover targets) no longer make the display list inexact.

  • The detail tier now also builds marks that are only partly in view (a bar or disc whose centre is off-screen). It used to test the centre alone, so such marks disappeared on deep zoom.

  • Fixed: zooming a raster plot whose display list has a single paint with no fill (e.g. one-colour keyed segments) threw, and the marks vanished. The length-1 NA column arrives as null, which left the paint table empty.

  • Raster exports show the marks as they are drawn (VW-25). The toolbar’s SVG, PNG and clipboard exports used the overview mark PNG. So condition() colours, dimming and filter_by() (VW-22) were missing, and a zoomed export showed that PNG scaled up and blurred. When vellum’s display list covers every mark exactly, the export now redraws it at export resolution (at least 2x, or export_options(scale)), with the current style state, into one image over the current view. The detail tier’s nodes and the mark PNG are left out of the export, and the above-marks furniture and re-ticked labels still go on top. Without an exact list (older vellum, above max_marks, flagged marks) the export keeps the mark PNG.

  • PNG exports at export_options(scale) above 1 keep non-scaling strokes (axis-zoomed lines, rules and outlines) at their on-screen weight. Before, they came out scale times too thin.

  • Under axis zoom, unkeyed panel furniture keeps its size, as the keyed marks do (VW-26). A reference rule no longer thickens, an annotation’s text stays its size, anchored where it was placed, and an unkeyed point layer keeps its pixel size. This applies in SVG mode and to both raster furniture layers (below and above the marks). Text marks with a key get the same treatment. render_options(zoom_marks = "scale") keeps the old scaling.

  • The navigator’s mini-map now shows the furniture painted after the marks (a reference line or annotation drawn over the points in raster mode, VW-21). It cloned only the base svg, so that layer was missing (VW-27).

vellumwidget 0.13.1

  • Raster widgets ship vellumplot’s new default keys ("p1-1:l2:7", VP-55) as compactly as plain row numbers: the key column’s delta encoding now also covers integers after a text prefix, with the prefixes sent as runs. A 20k-point default-keyed scatter sends about 40 kB of keys instead of 300 kB.

vellumwidget 0.13.0

  • Building a big widget is faster (VR-16). The element table’s meta columns (tooltip, legend, cond, …) are read column-wise from one flattened index instead of scanning every element’s record once per field. At 200k keyed points this step drops from about 1.5 s to 0.4 s. With the matching vellum and vellumplot changes, as_widget() on a 200k-point keyed scatter takes about 1.6 s instead of 7 s. The payload is unchanged.

  • In raster mode, a reference line or annotation added after the points is drawn over them again (VW-21). The split render put all the furniture under the marks image, so mark_rule() or annotate() layered after mark_point() disappeared under the points. With a vellum that splits the furniture by paint order (layer = "unkeyed_above"), what was painted after the marks ships as its own SVG layer, stacked over the marks at every tier (image, zoomed canvas, detail nodes). It zooms with its panel and is part of the SVG/PNG export. It never takes the pointer, so hovering and clicking still reach the marks underneath. With an older vellum it is drawn as before.

  • condition(), filter_by() and selection dimming show at every zoom in raster mode (VW-22). They used to take effect only once the detail tier’s SVG nodes existed; the overview image and the zoomed canvas drew every mark unchanged. The canvas now draws each mark from the display list with its key’s state: dimmed, in the condition’s if_false colour, or not at all when filtered out (also cross-filters and legend hide/mute). While any such state is active at the overview zoom, the canvas replaces the mark image. With more than 50,000 marks in view the redraw waits until the change settles (about 170 ms once for 200,000 points). Without a display list (an older vellum, or above render_options(max_marks = )), or when the list has marks it cannot reproduce, the image is shown unchanged and these states still apply only in the detail tier.

  • Zoom in far enough on a big plot and its marks become real, interactive SVG (VW-16). In raster mode with the display list, once a zoom settles with fewer than render_options(detail_marks = ) marks in view (default 3,000), the visible marks are built as keyed SVG nodes inside the zoomed panel, from their exact geometry and paint. Hover and click selection then style the marks themselves (no rings), condition() and filter_by() apply to them, and they are keyboard-focusable marks for screen readers. Panning or zooming within the detail tier rebuilds the nodes for the new view, keeping the selection. Zooming back out past 1.5 times the threshold returns to the canvas, and the selection shows as rings again. detail_marks = 0 turns it off. The swap happens once the view settles, not on every wheel tick.

  • A condition()’s if_false colour given as an R colour name ("grey80") is now sent to the browser as hex. The browser ignored such names, so the condition styled nothing (SVG mode too).

  • Zoomed-in big plots are drawn exactly, from a smaller payload (VW-15). With a vellum that has the marks-only display list (scene_display_list()), raster mode ships each keyed mark’s exact device-pixel geometry, paint and key instead of its bounding box. Once zoomed in, the canvas redraws the marks with their own shape (circle, square, triangle, diamond, plus, cross, star), rects and paths, fill, stroke, width, dash and alpha, in the engine’s paint order, where it used to draw plain dots in a colour read back from the image. The hit-test boxes are derived in the browser. The key column ships as integer differences when the keys are row numbers, and long runs of one value (every mark a “point”) as runs. A 20,000-point keyed scatter’s payload drops from 1.09 MB to 0.61 MB, a 200,000-point one from 8.3 MB to 3.9 MB. With more than 50,000 marks in view, the exact redraw waits until the zoom settles, and the image stands in meanwhile. Above render_options(max_marks = ) (default 500,000) no list ships: the widget keeps the bounding-box index and a message suggests vellumplot::mark_datashade() or vellumplot::mark_hex(). With an older vellum nothing changes. Marks the list cannot draw exactly (gradient or pattern paints, path clips, marks in a translucent group) keep their box and stay in the image.

  • Raster mode keeps real axes, so axis zoom, the navigator and linked zoom work on big plots (VW-14). With a vellum that has the split render (scene_svg(layer =) / scene_png(layer =)), raster mode no longer draws the whole scene as one image. The axes, gridlines, legend and text stay SVG, and only the keyed marks are a PNG, placed inside each panel’s zoomable group. Zooming re-ticks the real axes, facets zoom per panel, the range navigator is available, and bind_scale() / select_interval(bind = "scales") linked zoom now works in raster mode. Once zoomed in, the crisp point layer is drawn per panel and clipped to it, and the scaled mark image is hidden beneath it. render_options(text =) now applies to the furniture, so it no longer warns. SVG and PNG export give one image: furniture, the mark layer and the re-ticked axis labels (which an axis-zoomed export used to drop, in SVG mode too). With an older vellum (0.9.0) raster mode is unchanged.

  • A raster-mode widget ships less than half the data (VW-13). In raster mode (more than raster_threshold keyed marks) the element index, not the image, is most of the payload. It now ships in a compact encoding: a column with few distinct values (mark, a mark’s legend series) sends each value once plus a small integer code per mark, a column that only a handful of marks carry (the legend swatches’ tooltips) sends just those marks, and the bounding boxes are rounded outward to 1/100 px. A 20,000-point keyed scatter drops from 2.45 MB to 1.09 MB (gzip 0.90 to 0.48 MB), a 200,000-point one from 21.9 MB to 8.3 MB. The runtime decodes it back to the same per-mark records, and SVG mode is unchanged.

vellumwidget 0.12.0

  • Selection rings contrast with the plot, not the OS colour scheme (VW-20). The selection stroke, crosshair and colorbar wash switched to their light variants whenever the page was viewed in a dark colour scheme. On a white plot that made the ring near-white, and on a theme_dark() plot in light mode it stayed dark. The widget now reads the scene’s panel background (and the plot background for the colorbar wash) and picks dark ink for light backgrounds and light ink for dark ones (theme_dark(), theme_cyberpunk()), whatever the OS scheme. A selection colour set by the user (a mark’s selected_color) still wins.

  • A brush no longer blanks out a line it only partly covers (VW-19). A line, path or area drawn as one keyed element spans a whole series. A brush over part of it (a select_interval() brush, a plain brush or a lasso) used to select it, and the selected style restroked the line in the selection colour. With a dark colour scheme on a light plot that colour is near-white, so the overview line of an overview + detail disappeared. The partly covered line is now left as it is, much as Vega-Lite leaves a line under an interval brush unless a condition() styles it. It is still a member of the interval, so condition(), filter_by(), binds and input$<id>_brush keys see it as before, but it is not selected and not in input$<id>_selected. A brush that covers the whole line still selects it. Points, bars and segments keep today’s behaviour.

  • Linked views zoom per cell (VW-18). In a composition with a bind_scale() or a select_interval(bind = "scales"), every cell used to share one zoom: a wheel on the overview also moved the detail’s unbound axis, and a pan on the bound detail moved the overview. Each cell now keeps its own view. A wheel, pan or zoom-to-selection moves only the cell it starts in, a bound axis follows its selection, and reset returns every cell to its full view. input$<id>_zoom reports the last-zoomed cell’s view in x..h, and zoomed is TRUE while any cell is zoomed. Facets, and compositions without binds, still zoom together. Binds remain SVG-only: a raster render ignores them.

  • Zoomed axes show their gridlines and tick marks (VW-17). Under axis-aware zoom the re-ticked gridlines went in under vellumplot’s opaque panel background, so a zoomed panel showed none, and the static tick marks stayed in the scaled pan group and drifted off their breaks. The panel background now moves out of the pan group and the re-ticked grid sits on top of it; the background no longer scales with the zoom either. The static ticks are hidden along with the static labels and re-drawn at the new breaks in the theme’s stroke and length, and an axis line (theme_classic()) stays visible. Applies to facets, compositions and secondary axes alike.

  • Overview + detail: vellumplot::bind_scale() is enacted (F-15). Brushing an overview view zooms every panel bound to the brush to the brushed range on the bound axis, re-ticking its axes; clearing the brush resets it. The view the brush is drawn in never zooms itself, and in a composition a brush in another cell leaves the selection alone. Date and datetime axes convert between days and seconds, a discrete target zooms to the brushed levels, and log/sqrt/reversed axes map through their transform. input$<id>_zoom reports the bound range in panels and names the bound panels in bound. SVG mode with axis-aware zoom only.

  • vellumplot::select_interval(bind = "scales") (F-15). The selection is the view’s own pan/zoom: the settled visible range of its cell writes it (no brush band), resetting the zoom empties it, and the default drag is pan. A bind_scale() on another view then follows it (linked zoom), and condition() / filter_by() react to what is in view.

  • Panel descriptors carry the composition cell vellumplot now records, so a composition’s per-cell panels ("cell-2-panel-1-1", …) zoom and report individually. With vellumplot 0.14.1.9000 or later an aligned composition’s panels are described and pannable, so compositions get axis-aware zoom too.

  • Selection, hover and focus rings show in full on a point drawn as one element (VW-12). vellum is moving a keyed point with a solid fill and an undashed solid stroke from a fill element plus a fill="none" stroke twin to one element carrying both paints, halving the DOM nodes of a scatter. The ring rules painted the stroke under the fill (paint-order: stroke fill), which on one element hides the inner half of the ring; they now use paint-order: normal, so the ring looks the same on both outputs. The widget works with either: hover, selection and conditional colours act on every node of a key, and a condition recolours the fill and stroke a node actually uses.

vellumwidget 0.11.0

  • Linked widgets follow a changed group and are freed when removed (VW-5). After a Shiny re-render with a new group (or crosstalk group), a widget published to the new group but kept listening on the old one. It now leaves the old group and joins the new one, closing its old crosstalk handles. A widget whose element is removed from the page (a re-render, renderUI()) leaves the linking bus and closes its crosstalk handles instead of lingering.

  • Hover in open space finds the right mark when zoomed (VW-3). The client-to-scene fit behind nearest-mark hover is now made per data panel, from that panel’s own marks, and ignores legend swatches and hidden or filtered marks. Before, one fit across every mark and the legend went wrong once axis zoom scaled the data but not the legend, and in faceted plots. The fit is cached until the view, the widget size, a re-render or a legend/filter change invalidates it, so a hover frame no longer scans every element and forces four layouts.

  • as_widget()’s settings are grouped into option helpers. The flat arguments move into four helpers, each validating its own arguments:

    Old argument New
    tooltip_delay, tooltip_follow, tooltip_sticky, tooltip_style tooltip = tooltip_options(delay, follow, sticky, style)
    export_filename, export_scale export = export_options(filename, scale)
    navigator_height navigator = navigator_options(height)
    mode, raster_threshold, text render = render_options(mode, raster_threshold, text)

    navigator still takes TRUE/FALSE. The old names keep working but are deprecated: each warns once per session. Passing an option object together with its own old names (say tooltip = tooltip_options() and tooltip_delay = 250) is an error. as_widget() drops from 24 formals to 18, and the export filename and scale now always reach the payload ("plot" and 1 by default, the runtime’s own fallbacks) (R-13).

  • Zoom follow-ups for facets, secondary axes and time zones (VW-10).

    • input$<id>_zoom gains panels, a list keyed by panel id with each panel’s visible data range (list(x=, y=, panel=)), so a faceted plot reports what every facet shows. Under plain viewBox zoom a panel outside the view reports NULL. Single-panel plots keep data as before, so existing code is unaffected.
    • Axis-aware zoom re-ticks secondary axes (sec_axis() / dup_axis()) instead of hiding them. The transform is read back from the static axis’s own labels: exact for a linear transform, interpolated between the static breaks otherwise. A shared prefix or suffix ("$", " km") and thousands separators carry over. An axis whose labels are not plain numbers stays hidden under zoom.
    • Datetime ticks get their own UTC offset when the static labels show a daylight-saving change. Such an axis is matched to an IANA time zone that reproduces its labels (the viewer’s zone is tried first), so zooming into a DST change no longer shifts labels by an hour. An axis that one fixed offset explains keeps that offset.

  • as_widget() now checks every argument up front and fails with an error that names the argument. Before, raster_threshold = NA crashed with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”, tooltip_delay = "abc" sent NA to the browser, and group = 1:3 sent an array. Flags must be TRUE or FALSE, sizes and delays non-negative numbers, group / alt / export_filename / elementId single strings, and tooltip_style a named list of its four known fields (an unknown field is now an error, not silently dropped) (VW-6).

  • vellumwidget_proxy() works with module ids (VW-7). The proxy looked up its widget with a bare "#" + id selector, so an output id holding . or : (common inside Shiny modules) silently matched nothing. The id is now escaped with CSS.escape(), with a built-in fallback where the browser lacks it.

  • Hover is cheaper while the pointer stays on one mark (VW-4). A pointer move that resolves to the same hovered mark and highlight set now only moves the tooltip; it no longer clears and re-applies the highlight classes, re-runs the condition() pass or rebuilds the tooltip. Moving through empty space no longer re-clears a plot with nothing hovered. On a 3000-mark plot with one hover condition, 50 moves over the same mark went from about 245 ms to about 1 ms in the jsdom benchmark.

vellumwidget 0.10.0

  • Interval selections brush a data range. A plot that declares vellumplot::select_interval() now turns the brush into that named selection, and condition() / filter_by() react to it as they do to a point selection. Membership is by data value: the brushed pixels are converted to a data range through the panel’s scale (continuous, log10/sqrt/reverse, date, datetime, or the covered categories of a discrete axis) and each element’s own data values are tested, so a brush in one facet selects matching rows in every facet. An x-only (or y-only) brush leaves a band across the full panel that stays on the data through pan and zoom; clicking empty space or pressing Escape clears it. Members are reported in input$<id>_selected; input$<id>_brush gains selection and interval, and goes to NULL when the brush is cleared. When the scales cannot be inverted (a raw scene, a composition, a custom transform) the brush falls back to selecting what it covers on screen. Needs no new as_widget() option, and works without Shiny.

  • Axis-aware zoom now re-ticks log, date, datetime and discrete axes, and faceted plots. Before, any of these fell back to scaling the whole scene. Log10 axes tick decades, then 1-3 or 1-2-5 subdivisions as you zoom in, with vellumplot’s static labels. Date and datetime axes tick on calendar boundaries (years down to seconds) and keep the axis’s own date_labels format until the step needs a finer one; a datetime axis drawn in a local time zone ticks on that zone’s clock. Discrete and binned axes keep the categories still in view. In a faceted plot every panel zooms about the matching point and re-ticks its own axes, labelling only the outer panels as the static plot does. The panels payload now carries each axis’s static breaks and labels.

  • Under axis-aware zoom, wheel and pinch zooms stay anchored under the cursor once the view is already zoomed. The client-to-plot mapping used the zoomed view where the frame shows the base one, so the anchor drifted.

vellumwidget 0.9.1

  • Hovering or clicking a polygon’s hole no longer hits the polygon. The runtime decided “inside” per ring, so a point inside any ring, a hole included, counted as on the shape. It now decides once across all of an element’s rings under the rule the shape is filled with (even-odd or nonzero winding), as vellum’s vl_nearest() does from vellum 0.7.2. The payload’s geometry block gains an eo column, sent only when some element is even-odd.

  • Hexagons and pie/donut sectors now hover and click by their outline instead of their bounding box. vellum 0.7.2 reports their geometry.

  • Click-to-source now shows each mark’s own rows, including marks from a layer with its own data. vellumplot tags every element with the table its rows refer to, and the widget now ships each layer’s table (fields, plus the rows when inspect_source(values = TRUE)) next to the plot data. Clicking a mark from a layer drawn with data = lists that layer’s fields and rows instead of nothing. The vellum:source event and input$<id>_source gain a source entry ("plot" or "layer:<i>") and report that table’s fields. This supersedes the 0.9.0 stopgap that left such marks out of the popover. Plot-data marks are unchanged, and an element without a source tag (an older vellumplot) still reads the plot data.

vellumwidget 0.9.0

  • Click-to-source no longer shows the wrong rows for a layer with its own data. The popover looks every element’s rows up in the plot’s data, but a layer drawn from its own data = indexes that layer’s table, so clicking one of its marks listed unrelated rows of the plot data. vellumplot now tags each element with the table its rows refer to, and elements from a layer’s own data are left out of the popover instead of answering with the wrong rows.

  • Security fix: the click-to-source popover no longer parses data as HTML. The popover that inspect_source() opens on a click was assembled as an HTML string and inserted with innerHTML. Field names and row values only passed through a regex that strips complete <...> tags, so an unterminated tag in the data, such as <img src=x onerror=alert(1) //, survived and ran as script in the viewer’s page. The popover is now built element by element with textContent, the way the accessible data table already is, so every value is shown as literal text. Markup in a value (<b>bold</b>) now appears as written instead of being stripped.

  • A polygon with a hole is now hit-tested exactly, not approximately. A path element ships every ring’s vertices concatenated, and the runtime had no way to tell where one ring ended – so it read the whole run as ONE closed ring. That invents a phantom edge from each ring’s last vertex to the next ring’s first, and closes the last ring back to the very first vertex. Exact for a single-ring path (a plain sf polygon, the common case), an approximation for a polygon with a hole or a multipart feature, and the error is not small: on a square-with-a-hole fixture the old reading put a point 20 px outside the shape at 90 px away, and called the shape’s own centre a miss.

    vellum::element_geometry() gained a ring column in 0.7.0, so the payload now carries the ring boundaries (nr, rl) and the runtime measures each ring separately. It follows the engine’s own rule – a path’s distance is the minimum over its rings, each measured as filled, so being inside any ring is a hit and the fill rule does not enter into it. Client-side answers now match vl_nearest() exactly on the same scene.

    Both columns are omitted when every element is a single ring, so the usual payload does not grow, and a widget saved by an older build keeps working on the one-ring reading.

  • Bug fix: data marks are no longer drawn offset from their own coordinates. Under axis_zoom/zoom_marks = "fixed" (both default), the constant-size counter-scale is applied as an inline CSS transform, which outranks the SVG transform presentation attribute. Panel marks are positioned by that attribute (a panel-offset matrix), so the counter-scale replaced their placement and every glyph rendered at its untranslated geometry — displaced from the scene by the panel origin. The widget therefore showed the wrong data coordinates, and disagreed with the PNG and PDF of the same scene.

    The inline transform now carries the node’s own placement ahead of the counter-scale, so position and constant size both hold. transform-origin resolves the scale about the glyph’s own centre and translations commute with that, so the composition is exact for the translate-only matrices vellum emits.

    The visible symptom was a crosshair that missed the mark it was tracking: drawCrosshair() works in scene space (correctly), while hit-testing calibrates against the marks’ real rendered positions, so hover was right and the guide rule was not. Both agree again.

    This is the same clobbering as the 0.8.0 legend-swatch fix, which assumed data points “carry absolute coordinates” and so restricted the counter-scale to marks inside the pannable region. Marks inside that region carry a positioning transform too, so excluding the outside was not enough.

vellumwidget 0.8.0

Requires vellum >= 0.6.6, which fixes the coordinate space element_geometry() reports in — the exact hit-testing below is built on it.

  • The raster base image is now rendered at 2× for HiDPI screens. A widget is always viewed at screen resolution, and a 1× image stretched by the browser is visibly soft on a retina display. scene_png(scale = 2) multiplies dpi while holding physical size, so the image carries two pixels per device pixel while the SVG shell stays in device pixels — the space the element bounding boxes and panel rectangles live in, so nothing about hit-testing or pan/zoom changes.

    No new argument: raster mode is chosen precisely when the SVG alternative would be enormous, so the extra bytes are noise against what they replace (at 30,000 keyed points, 446 KB → 877 KB, versus a 14.7 MB per-element SVG). The dense end is cheaper at 2×, not dearer — a saturated canvas compresses better.

    The shell’s dimensions now come from the scene rather than from the image, via vellum::vl_convert(). Halving a scaled PNG re-rounds and drifted by a pixel on a fractional page size, which would have put a small but systematic offset between the drawn frame and the bounding-box space picking uses.

  • Exact hit-testing: picking now measures to the mark, not to its box. The payload carries each keyed element’s true vertices in device pixels (vellum::element_geometry(), computed once at build time); the Flatbush R-tree still shortlists candidates by bounding box — a box distance is never greater than the true distance, so nothing in range is missed — and the shortlist is then ranked by distance to the actual shape. What changes:

    • Graph edges are hoverable. An edge’s box is the whole rectangle its endpoints span, so a box-distance “nearest” matched it from anywhere inside that rectangle; edges had to be excluded from the open-space snap entirely. They are now measured to the line and compete on their merits.
    • A diagonal is no longer matched from the far corner of its box. On a four-series line chart whose boxes each cover ~91% of the panel, a cursor on a line picks that line — where previously two or more series were tied at box-distance zero at 39 of 40 probe positions.
    • A click inside a filled region hits the region, at distance zero, rather than snapping to whichever border happens to be nearest.
    • Round marks are measured to the disc, not to the square around it.

    Only the kinds whose shape is not their box (segment, line, polygon, path) are shipped; a point’s disc and a label’s box are reconstructed from the bounding box the payload already carries, so the dense scatter — where payload size actually bites — pays nothing for this. Above 500,000 vertices the block is dropped with a message and picking falls back to boxes.

    Brush and lasso are unchanged: a box is the right answer for a rectangular brush, which is what it was always for.

  • Raster-mode widgets no longer touch disk. The base image is now encoded with vellum::scene_png(), which returns the PNG bytes, instead of rendering to a tempfile() and reading it back. Widget output is unchanged.

  • Animated plots as widgets. as_widget() now accepts a keyframe animation from vellumplot::animate() and embeds it as a self-contained animated SVG — resolution-independent and honouring prefers-reduced-motion (both handled inside the SVG by vellum). It plays on its own through the runtime’s existing inline-SVG mount; since the marks move every frame there is no per-element interaction index (no hover/brush) and no raster canvas.

  • Fix: click-to-source did nothing for single-row groups. A grob backed by one data row had its rows auto-unboxed to a scalar in the payload, so the runtime’s rows.length check skipped it (no event, no popover) — e.g. every single-county region of a choropleth. The payload now forces arrays, and the runtime coerces a scalar defensively.

  • Click-to-source. When a plot opts in with vellumplot::inspect_source(), clicking a mark surfaces the source data rows behind it: the widget reads the compiled scene’s provenance (keyed by each grob’s data-vellum-id), fires a bubbling vellum:source DOM event (detail = id, rows, fields, and values when inspect_source(values = TRUE)), sets input$<id>_source under Shiny, and shows a small values popover. Opt-in rides the spec, so it adds no as_widget() argument and no payload weight to a plain widget.

vellumwidget 0.7.0

  • Bug fix: hover snapped to the wrong mark on a scaled plot. When the svg was rendered at a different size than its viewBox implies (the widget’s max-width:100%, the RStudio Viewer pane, an embedded/saveWidget page), hover highlighted a mark offset from the cursor (usually up-and-left); click was unaffected because it uses the DOM target. The client→scene hit-test mapping relied on getScreenCTM() / viewBox math, which can disagree with how the content is actually laid out when the svg carries width/height attributes. Hit-testing (hover, brush, lasso) now calibrates the transform from the real rendered positions of the marks themselves versus their known scene bboxes — exact under any viewBox / attribute / CSS-scale / zoom combination. Tooltip anchoring uses the mark’s own rendered position.

  • Breaking: interaction is now declared in the plot, not on as_widget(). The interaction-intent arguments have been removed — hover_color, selected_color, dim_opacity (now vellumplot::condition()), and the hover/select/brush/lasso/tooltip/nearest/zoom/axis_zoom/ zoom_marks toggles (now on by default — interactive-by-default). The signature drops from ~36 to 24 arguments. Per-plot interaction (highlight, filter, cross-filter) travels with the spec via vellumplot::select_point()/select_interval()/condition()/filter_by(). Requires vellumplot (>= 0.6.0.9000). (hover_mode, crosshair, legend_click, select_mode, and the tooltip-appearance args remain until their spec equivalents land.)

  • Declarative interactivity: cross-view filtering. A selection defined on one cell of a composition and referenced by filter_by() on another now cross-filters — brush/select the source cell and the linked cell narrows to the matching rows, matched by a cross-view join id. The source cell stays fully visible; only the target cell hides (scoped by per-cell-unique keys). All in one widget runtime, no server round-trip.

  • Declarative interactivity: filters. A vellumplot plot that declares filter_by(selection) now hides everything outside the selection when that selection’s gesture fires — reusing the cross-filter path. Driven entirely by the plot spec (no as_widget() argument). Single-view for now; the cross-view form (brush one panel, filter another) follows.

  • Declarative interactivity: conditional encodings. as_widget() now reads the interaction model a vellumplot plot declares (select_point() / condition()) off the compiled spec and enacts it on the frozen scene. A hover- or click-driven selection with a condition() on an aesthetic keeps selection members at their if_true style and applies if_false to non-members (an explicit colour, or the theme dim as a spotlight) — reverting when the selection empties. No new as_widget() argument: the behaviour travels with the plot. (Filters, cross-view, and scale binds follow.)

vellumwidget 0.6.0

  • Bug fix: legend swatches no longer jump off-screen under axis-aware zoom. With axis_zoom/zoom_marks = "fixed" (both default), the constant-size counter- scale was applied to every glyph mark, including discrete legend swatches. Because a swatch is positioned by a transform attribute (unlike data points, which carry absolute coordinates), the inline counter-scale overrode that attribute and flung the swatch to a corner. The counter-scale is now restricted to marks inside the pannable data region, so legend swatches stay put.

  • Axis-aware zoom (axis_zoom, default TRUE). Wheel/drag zoom scales only the plot’s data region and re-ticks the axes for the visible range — holding the frame (axes, titles, legend) in place the way a charting library zooms, rather than scaling the whole scene like an image. Hit-testing (hover/brush/lasso), the crosshair, and the input$<id>_zoom data range all follow the zoomed data region. Applies to a single linear cartesian panel (continuous identity/reverse axes) rendered as SVG; plots with log/date/discrete axes, several panels, or in raster mode silently fall back to the ordinary whole-scene zoom, so it is safe to leave on. Set axis_zoom = FALSE for the plain whole-scene zoom. Built on vellum’s pannable-panel contract (vl_viewport(pannable=)) and the panel scale metadata vellumplot emits (needs the current development vellum/vellumplot).

  • Constant-size markers on zoom (zoom_marks, default "fixed"). Under axis-aware zoom, glyph marks (points, circles, hexagons, sector wedges) now keep their original pixel size and only their positions re-map — so points stay round and don’t stretch into ellipses under the navigator’s x-only zoom, the way a charting library zooms. Positional marks (bars, error bars, lines, areas) still scale with the data; their stroke width is held constant. Set zoom_marks = "scale" for the old behaviour where glyphs grow with the zoom (useful to read density). Applies to SVG axis-aware zoom and the raster crisp-point layer.

  • Interactive continuous colorbar filter (visualMap). When a vellumplot plot maps a continuous color scale, its colorbar becomes a range filter: drag the two handles on the gradient bar to a value range and marks whose colour value falls outside it fade out (and drop out of hover/brush hit-testing); double-click the bar to reset. The selected range is reported to Shiny as input$<id>_colorfilter = c(lo, hi) (NULL at the full range). Automatic — no argument to set — whenever the plot has a continuous colorbar (needs the current development vellumplot; SVG mode). Discrete/binned colour legends keep their existing click-to-hide interaction.

  • Tooltip polish. as_widget() gains tooltip_delay (ms to wait before the tooltip appears — the highlight is immediate, only the tooltip waits), tooltip_follow (TRUE, the default, tracks the cursor; FALSE anchors above the mark), and tooltip_sticky (the tooltip accepts pointer events and lingers briefly on leave, so tooltips containing links/buttons are usable). The tooltip also now auto-flips below the cursor when there isn’t room above and clamps horizontally so it doesn’t overflow the widget.

  • Overview navigator (navigator = TRUE). An opt-in strip below the plot that renders the whole scene in miniature with a draggable, resizable window marking the visible x-range: drag the window to pan, drag a handle to zoom. Zoom is x-only — the selected x-range fills the width while the full y-range stays on screen (a time-series range selector). With axis_zoom (the default) it is rendered through the axis-aware zoom, so the x-axis re-ticks crisply; otherwise the view stretches horizontally. It stays two-way in sync with the main view — wheel/keyboard/brush, the toolbar, and linked-group pan/zoom all move the window, and moving the window drives them. Useful for scrubbing long series. navigator_height sets the strip height (default 56px). Client-side; off by default.

  • Linked pan/zoom across a group. Widgets sharing a group already linked selection and hover; now panning or zooming one moves the others to the same view. The view is shared as a fraction of each widget’s own extent (over the same client-side bus, no Shiny/crosstalk), so linked plots of different sizes — small multiples — stay aligned. Reset links too.

  • Brush and view now report data-space coordinates, not just pixels. When the plot carries a cartesian scale (any vellumplot plot), input$<id>_brush gains the brushed region’s data-space bounds x0d,y0d,x1d,y1d (plus the panel name) alongside the existing device-pixel rectangle, and input$<id>_zoom gains data = list(x=, y=, panel=), the visible range in data coordinates. This reads the per-panel scale descriptors vellumplot now attaches to the scene (requires the current development vellum (>= 0.4.0.9000) and vellumplot); a raw vellum scene or a non-cartesian coordinate system reports device-pixel fields only, as before. Date/time axes report the numeric epoch (days for Date, seconds for POSIXct), which you map back with as.Date() / .POSIXct(). The fields describe the visual axes (under coord_flip(), x0d is the plot’s y aesthetic); a discrete axis reports fractional band positions; and an axis built with a custom scales::transform_*() object (beyond identity / log10 / sqrt / reverse) is omitted from the data-space fields rather than reported wrong. (Groundwork for axis-aware zoom.)

  • Fix: cross-filtered and legend-hidden marks were still hit-testable. A display-tier cross-filter (crosstalk or vw_filter()) and a legend legend_click = "hide" toggle set the marks to display:none, but they stayed in the spatial index — so a nearest-mark hover could still tooltip a hidden datum, and a brush or lasso could re-select filtered-out points (propagating the selection back to linked/crosstalk views). Keyboard traversal already skipped hidden marks; hover, brush, lasso, and raster click-snap now do too, via a single “inert” guard. Muted (not hidden) legend series stay interactive.

  • Freehand lasso-select. A third drag mode alongside brush and pan (default on; disable with as_widget(lasso = FALSE)). The toolbar’s mode button now cycles brush → lasso → pan, and it appears whenever at least two drag modes are enabled. Drag a loop and every mark whose centre falls inside it is selected — hit-tested with a point-in-polygon check over the Flatbush spatial index, so it stays fast on large scenes. It reports through input$<id>_brush like the box brush, with a lasso = TRUE flag and the loop’s bounding box.

  • Widgets report their current view to Shiny (input$<id>_zoom). After a zoom/pan settles — wheel, drag-pan release, pinch, keyboard, reset, zoom-to-selection, or a vw_zoom() proxy call — the widget publishes list(x=, y=, w=, h=, zoomed=): the current viewBox (device-px) and whether the view is zoomed in. A deduped state input, so a coordinated dashboard can react to what the user is looking at. (Data-space limits await axis/scale metadata in the scene contract.)

  • Legend click-to-hide and double-click-to-isolate. as_widget() gains a legend_click argument. The default "select" is unchanged (clicking a discrete-legend swatch selects its series). "hide" turns the legend into a visibility toggle — a single click hides or shows the series, a double-click isolates it (hides every other series; double-click again to restore all) — the reflexive legend interaction from plotly / ECharts / Highcharts. "mute" is the same but dims the series rather than removing it (keeping its layout). Hovering a swatch still highlights its series under every policy, and hidden series drop out of hover/tooltip hit-testing. Works with keyboard (Enter/Space on a focused swatch toggles) and is independent of the crosstalk cross-filter (the two never clobber each other). Entirely client-side.

  • Shared (unified) hover tooltips and a crosshair. as_widget() gains a hover_mode argument. The default "closest" is unchanged (hover shows the single nearest mark), but "x" (or "y") turns on a unified hover: every mark sharing the hovered x (or y) position is highlighted at once and listed together in one tooltip box — the shared readout multi-series line and time-series charts expect, where you want every series’ value at the cursor’s x rather than one point. A companion crosshair argument (default FALSE) draws a guide rule at the hovered position: a vertical rule at the shared x in "x" mode, a horizontal one in "y" mode, and a full cross through the mark in "closest" mode. Both are entirely client-side and need no extra scene metadata — the mark positions come straight from the element index — so they work on any keyed vellumplot plot or raw vellum scene, and in raster mode. Unified hover snaps along its axis so the readout tracks the cursor anywhere in the plot; the hover Shiny input still reports the single nearest (primary) mark, so the read-back contract is unchanged.

  • Fix: hover/selection feedback rings were drawn offset from the mark. When the widget container was larger than the plot’s rendered box — which happens routinely, as htmlwidgets stamps an explicit height on the container and a fluid layout can stretch its width — the feedback overlay filled the whole container while the base SVG only filled its aspect-locked box. The overlay’s viewBox then letterboxed (centred), so every hover/selection ring drew off the real mark: downward when the container was taller (e.g. 68px low for a 520px-tall container over a 384px plot) and sideways when it was wider. It looked like the wrong mark was picked. Hit-testing itself was always correct; only the visual feedback was displaced. The svg and its overlays now share a shrink-to-fit stage, so the overlay tracks the svg box exactly at any container size.

vellumwidget 0.5.0

  • text argument on as_widget(). Choose how text is written into the SVG, passed through to vellum::scene_svg(): "native" (the default) emits selectable <text> referencing system fonts — smaller when the page has the font, post-processable, and better for accessibility and LLMs — while "outline" emits pixel-faithful, font-independent glyph paths. Applies to the per-element SVG path only; in raster mode text is baked into the base image and the argument is ignored (with a warning if set explicitly) (#1).

  • New articles. Two articles document the features added since 0.4.0: Linking views with crosstalk (coordinating a widget with DT / plotly / leaflet and crosstalk’s filter_* inputs) and Very large scenes (raster mode, the spatial index, the columnar payload, and crisp zoom).

  • Crisp zoom in raster mode. When you zoom into a raster-mode plot, the base image used to upscale and blur. The widget now redraws the points sharply on a <canvas> overlay while zoomed in — sampling each point’s colour straight from the rendered image and its position/size from the element index, so the crisp layer matches what vellum drew. It engages only when zoomed in (the faithful, anti-aliased base image still shows at the full view), redraws just the points in view, and degrades gracefully to the image alone where a 2D canvas context isn’t available. Entirely client-side; no change to the payload or to small/moderate (SVG-mode) plots.

  • Very large scatterplots are navigable (raster mode). as_widget() gains a mode argument ("auto" / "svg" / "raster"). In "auto" (the default), a scene with more than raster_threshold keyed elements (default 20000) is drawn once as a single embedded image instead of one SVG node per element, and all interaction — hover tooltips + highlight, click/brush select, pan/zoom — is driven client-side from the element index (bounding boxes + keys) rather than the DOM. A 150k-point keyed scatter that previously produced a ~75 MB SVG with 150,000 DOM nodes now ships as a ~0.8 MB image plus a compact index, with a handful of DOM nodes, and stays smooth to hover and pan. Small and moderate plots are unchanged (they keep the per-element SVG). Trade-offs in raster mode: per-element grammar colours, per-mark screen-reader focus, and display-tier cross-filtering don’t apply (there are no per-element nodes), and a zoomed-in view is a scaled raster until re-rendered. Adds a dependency on base64enc.

  • Smoother hover, brush, and pan on large plots. Two client-side changes lift the per-interaction cost that made big scatterplots laggy:

    • Spatial index. Nearest-mark hover and rectangular brush now hit-test against a Flatbush R-tree (O(log n) / O(k)) instead of scanning every element each time. The nearest-mark scan runs on every pointer move, so this is the change you feel most.
    • Cheaper hover dim. Above a threshold, hovering dims the plot once (via the holder’s opacity) and re-draws the hovered marks crisply in a small overlay — O(hovered) — instead of restyling every element via CSS (O(n)), which forced a full-scene style recalc on each hover. Small and moderate plots keep the exact previous per-mark dim. (Phase 2 of vellum’s big-data interactivity plan.)

  • Much faster, smaller payload for large plots (columnar element table). The keyed-element metadata as_widget() embeds is now serialised in a columnar form (one array per field) instead of one JSON object per element. This is a transparent wire-format change — the widget behaves identically — but it removes the per-element serialisation cost that dominated at large N. On a 150,000-point keyed scatter the payload build + serialise dropped from ~24 s / 89 MB to ~0.4 s / 12 MB (~60x faster), so a big interactive scatter is no longer choked by payload generation. Small and moderate plots are unaffected. (This is Phase 1 of vellum’s big-data interactivity plan; the browser-side DOM/hover work for truly huge scatters follows in later phases.)

  • Error bars and boxplots are interactive. Now that vellumplot keys these statistical marks, the widget hovers, tooltips, clicks/selects, and brushes them as units: an error bar’s bar + caps, or a box’s rect + median + whiskers, all light up and select together because they share one data-key (outliers stay individually addressable). Brush selection no longer double-counts a mark whose key spans several SVG elements — input$<id>_brush$keys reports each such key once. No runtime change was needed for the core behaviour; it already grouped every node sharing a key.

vellumwidget 0.4.0

  • Server-to-client proxy (vellumwidget_proxy()). A Shiny app can now drive an already-rendered widget from the server without re-rendering it — no renderVellumwidget() round-trip, no lost pan/zoom. Get a handle with vellumwidget_proxy(outputId) (inside an observe()), then pipe it through the verbs:
    • vw_select() / vw_clear_selection() — set or clear the selection (projects across hover_group and propagates to linked / crosstalk widgets, exactly like a user click, and updates input$<id>_selected);
    • vw_filter() / vw_clear_filter() — cross-filter the widget (show only the given keys, dim the rest; display tier, data untouched);
    • vw_zoom() / vw_reset_zoom() — frame a set of keys, or restore the full view.
    All keys are the element data_ids — the same identifiers you read back through input$<id>_selected. This completes the two-way Shiny story begun with the input read-back in 0.3.0; see the expanded Using vellumwidget in Shiny article.

vellumwidget 0.3.0

  • Adopted vellum’s renamed vl_* graphics primitives (grid collision fix).

  • Shiny input read-back. A widget rendered with vellumwidgetOutput() now reports the user’s interactions to the server as reactive inputs keyed by the output id: input$<id>_selected (selected keys, state), input$<id>_click (list(key=), event), input$<id>_hover (hovered key or NULL, state), and input$<id>_brush (list(keys=, x0=, y0=, x1=, y1=), event). Values are element data keys, so they map straight back to your data. Emitted only in a live Shiny session — a static render is unchanged and produces no input traffic. See the new Using vellumwidget in Shiny article. (Driving the widget from the server — a vellumwidget_proxy() — is a planned follow-up.)

  • Accessibility (a11y = TRUE, on by default). The interactive widget is now keyboard- and screen-reader-navigable, not a mute image:

    • the SVG is announced as an interactive chart (role="graphics-document" + aria-roledescription), labelled from the scene’s title/description (which vellumplot sets automatically) or an explicit as_widget(alt =);
    • every mark is a focusable graphics-symbol with a roving tabindex — arrow keys move between marks, Enter/Space toggles selection, Escape exits;
    • a polite aria-live region announces the focused / selected mark;
    • a visually-hidden data table lists every mark for assistive tech. All gated on a11y; a11y = FALSE restores the previous output exactly. See the vellumplot Accessibility article.

vellumwidget 0.2.0

Interaction-depth release (ROADMAP §4).

  • Rich tooltips. Tooltip text now renders as safe HTML: an author-built tooltip = (e.g. via glue()) may use <b>/<i>/<br> for bold/italic/ line breaks. Data values are escaped and only inert, attribute-free tags are honoured — no scripts, handlers, or attributes (no XSS). New as_widget(tooltip_style =) themes the tooltip box (background/color/fontsize/ max_width).
  • Touch + keyboard. The widget is driven by pointer events, so pan/brush/ hover work with mouse, touch, and pen from one path; a two-finger pinch zooms. With the widget focused, arrow keys pan, +/- zoom, and 0 resets.
  • Configurable export. as_widget(export_filename =, export_scale =) set the download filename base and a hi-res PNG multiplier; exports capture the current (zoomed/panned) view. A “copy PNG to clipboard” toolbar button appears where the Clipboard API is available.
  • Large-N performance. Hover/selection highlighting uses a per-render key→node cache instead of a querySelectorAll per key, and the nearest-mark hover scan is throttled to one per animation frame.
  • New “Interactive widgets: a tour” article.

Deferred: a spatial index for hit-testing (the DOM cost was the real bottleneck, now cached; bbox scans are cheap and datashade collapses huge clouds to a raster); coordinated zoom across linked widgets and URL deep-linking; PDF export.

vellumwidget 0.1.0

First release. vellumwidget turns a vellum scene or a vellumplot plot into a self-contained, client-side interactive HTML widget via a single terminal as_widget() pipe — no Shiny, no server round-trip. Everything below ships in this first release.

Features

  • as_widget() compiles a vellumplot plot or a raw vellum scene and bundles its SVG + scene_model() element table into an htmlwidget.
  • Hover — tooltip (from the declared tooltip, falling back to the key) and highlight with inverse-dim; a hovered element’s hover_group highlights the whole group. Hover snaps to the nearest mark when the cursor isn’t directly over one.
  • Click — select (single / multiple modes); every element sharing a key toggles together.
  • Brush — drag a rectangle to select every element it covers.
  • Pan / zoom — mouse wheel and pan-mode drag reframe the SVG viewBox, plus zoom-to-selection and reset.
  • Toolbar (on hover) — brush/pan mode toggle, zoom-to-selection, reset zoom, download SVG, download PNG, fullscreen.
  • Everything is opt-outable via as_widget() arguments (tooltip/hover/select/brush/zoom/toolbar/nearest).
  • Legend interaction. For a discrete color/shape scale on an interactive plot, each legend swatch drives its whole data series: hovering a swatch highlights the series (the swatch stays lit), clicking it selects the series (and links across views / crosstalk). Automatic — no extra arguments.
  • Linked views. as_widget(group=) links vellumwidget widgets client-side (no dependency): selecting/brushing in one highlights the same data keys in the others, projecting by hover_group (select one, select the series). as_widget(crosstalk = SharedData) bridges to the crosstalk ecosystem (plotly / leaflet / DT and filter_* inputs) via a SelectionHandle + FilterHandle; a crosstalk filter hides the non-matching marks (display-tier cross-filter). crosstalk is a Suggests, loaded only when used.
  • Customisable interaction styling, at two composing levels:
    • Widget theme — as_widget(hover_color=, selected_color=, dim_opacity=) sets the look for the whole plot (any R or CSS colour).
    • Per-element grammar — vellumplot marks’ hover_color/selected_color (constant or column-mapped) style each element individually and override the theme. Both use CSS variables with a defaults ← theme ← per-element cascade.

The JS runtime is TypeScript in srcts/, bundled by esbuild into the committed inst/htmlwidgets/vellumwidget.js (so the R package installs with no Node).
